newsitem.title: USA: First quarter 1997 magnesium shipments best ever.
newsitem.headline: First quarter 1997 magnesium shipments best ever.

text.p: Primary magnesium shipments in the first quarter reached 79,800 tonnes, the best ever and beating the previous record of 76,900 tonnes set in the second quarter of 1995, the International Magnesium Association said.

The first quarter shipments comprised of 55,700 tonnes produced in Brazil, Canada, France, Norway and U.S., and an estimated 18,700 tonnes exported from the Commonwealth of Independent States and China, and 5,400 tonnes drawn from inventory.
The CIS and China continue to increase their market share, up from 15 percent in 1994 to 23 percent in the first quarter of 1997, the IMA reported.
Aluminum alloying shipments fell 2,900 tonnes in the first quarter to 34,600 tonnes, but were up 300 tonnes from the fourth quarter of 1996, and accounted for 43 percent of shipments.

Desulfurization shipments rose 2,000 tonnes to 12,000 tonnes, and up 2,700 tonnes from the fourth quarter of last year. Much of the rise was in Western Europe. This sector, which involves purifying steel, accounts for 15 percent of primary magnesium shipments.

Die-casting shipments were up 7,200 tonnes at 22,500 tonnes, and up 2,600 tonnes from the previous quarter. Shipments to this market - components for vehicles - accounted for 28 percent of the total shipments.
However, primary magnesium production of 55,700 tonnes in the first quarter (excluding China, CIS and Israel) was down 9,500 tonnes, and off 6,100 tonnes from the previous quarter.
It was the lowest output for a quarter since the first quarter of 1994.
Inventory at the end of the first quarter totaled 36,700 tonnes, down 5,400 tonnes from the end of the last quarter of 1996.
